# XrealXRRuntime

**Inherits:** [`Node3D`](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_node3d.html)  
**Scene:** `addons/godot_xreal/features/xreal_xr_runtime.tscn`  
**Script:** `addons/godot_xreal/features/xreal_xr_runtime.gd`  

Bootstrap that drives an XROrigin3D hierarchy from the XREAL glasses.

The application owns the hierarchy, exactly as an OpenXR project does: its own XROrigin3D, XRCamera3D and XRController3D nodes, named however it likes. Add this component anywhere under or beside them and it attaches to what it finds, with no initialization code. Starting from nothing, instance xr_origin.tscn instead, which is that same hierarchy with this component already in it.

Attaching rather than owning is what makes a scene portable. The identical scene runs on an OpenXR headset with this component left out, where the OpenXR vendor plugin drives the same nodes. Nothing in this addon runs there.

On XREAL it also polls and fuses the native phone IMU, publishes touchpad state, converts glasses keys and app-owned phone UI controls into standard XR/InputMap events, and retains the raw XREAL signals as compatibility hooks.

## Properties

<a id="property-input_router"></a>

### input_router: XrealXRInputRouter = <unknown>

The bridge from controller trackers to XRController3D signals and InputMap actions.

<a id="property-xr_camera"></a>

### xr_camera: XRCamera3D

The head camera under that origin. Godot only moves an XRCamera3D for a viewport that renders through an XR interface, which the XREAL path never does, so this component mirrors the driver onto it.

<a id="property-xr_origin"></a>

### xr_origin: XROrigin3D

The tracking-space origin this component drives, resolved in _ready.

<a id="property-xr_origin_path"></a>

### xr_origin_path: NodePath

The XROrigin3D to drive. Leave it empty to search: an ancestor first, then this node's own children, then the rest of the tree.

## Signals

<a id="signal-backend_failed"></a>

### backend_failed(message: String)

The XREAL runtime could not start. `message` is the diagnostic also sent to push_error, readable later through get_last_error().

<a id="signal-display_started"></a>

### display_started()

The glasses display and tracking came up (re-emitted from the backend driver).

<a id="signal-key_event"></a>

### key_event(key: int, action: int)

A physical glasses key event, re-emitted from the backend driver. `key` and `action` use XrealHeadTracker's `KEY_*` and `ACTION_*` constants.

<a id="signal-wearing_changed"></a>

### wearing_changed(wearing: bool)

The wear sensor changed state, re-emitted from the backend driver.

## Methods

<a id="method-get_active_controller"></a>

### get_active_controller() -> XRController3D

Standard controller node currently representing the XREAL phone controller.

<a id="method-get_last_error"></a>

### get_last_error() -> String

The most recent initialization diagnostic, or "" once the backend is running. It also reports a second instance standing by, which is recoverable and so raises no backend_failed.

<a id="method-get_xreal_driver"></a>

### get_xreal_driver() -> Node3D

The XREAL backend driver, or null off device.

<a id="method-get_xreal_system"></a>

### get_xreal_system() -> Object

The shared XrealSystem facade, or null when the XREAL native runtime is inactive.

<a id="method-is_xreal_active"></a>

### is_xreal_active() -> bool

Whether the native XREAL backend driver is running.

<a id="method-pulse_controller_button"></a>

### pulse_controller_button(input_name: StringName)

Publish a one-frame app-owned button click through XRController3D and InputMap.

<a id="method-recenter"></a>

### recenter()

Recenter the phone controller and, on device, the head pose.

<a id="method-set_controller_axis"></a>

### set_controller_axis(value: Vector2, active: bool = true)

Feed or release an app-owned XREAL phone touchpad through the standard XR path.

<a id="method-set_controller_button"></a>

### set_controller_button(input_name: StringName, pressed: bool)

Feed a phone UI or another app-owned XREAL controller button through the standard XR path.

<a id="method-set_controller_hand"></a>

### set_controller_hand(is_right: bool)

Select which standard hand controller receives app-owned and native XREAL input.

<a id="method-set_hand_aim"></a>

### set_hand_aim(on: bool)

Let tracked hands aim and click, or stop them. On by default.

Turning it off hands every controller back to the phone at once: a hand mid-pinch lets go, and the hand that is not standing in for the phone loses its poses. An app whose UI moves off the glasses, to a phone screen say, wants that. Hands busy holding the phone would otherwise keep pointing a ray at the scene behind it and pinching by accident.

| Constant | Value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| <a id="constant-GROUP_RUNTIME"></a>`GROUP_RUNTIME` | `&"xreal_shared_xr_runtime"` | The runtime scene root joins this group; it detects duplicate runtime instances. |

| <a id="constant-XREAL_ACTION_CLICK"></a>`XREAL_ACTION_CLICK` | `1` | XrealHeadTracker.ACTION_CLICK: a single click of a glasses key. |
